coefficient_scope: GF(2), or any finite abelian group with a specified nonzero order-2 element after mapping coefficient 1 to it

claims.statement: For every rank-r binary matrix A on D columns, H_A has m=k=2^r P_A(1), minima count2^r B(A), min degree r, S=B(A), W=B(A)2^(2D).
claims.caveat: This construction uses parity; arbitrary groups without order-2 elements are not claimed.

claims.statement: For every alpha<log_2(1+sqrt(2)) and fixed C, some actual finite GF2 polynomial has W>C m^alpha k.
claims.method: E bases=kappa_r binom(D,r), kappa_r>1/4; m<=2^(D+r); D/r->3+2sqrt(2); binomial entropy bound and calculus.
claims.caveat: Limiting family is existential; no individual large matrix is claimed identified by this proof.
Counts obtained by subspace Mobius identities; expanded ANF or2^94 truth table was not materialized.

claims.statement: Ranks8,16,32,64,128 have certified finite existential exponent lower bounds1.18838,1.22577,1.24639,1.25786,1.26413 respectively.
claims.caveat: These rows give existence only and do not identify matrices.

claims.statement: An affine-coset indicator of codimension r with vanishing order r at allones decomposes into parity constraints on disjoint blocks, whose OR compositions cannot beat the earlier OR-pair exponent.
claims.caveat: Does not exclude lower vanishing orders or the new unique-solution predicate.

claims.statement: Given A, uniform conditional sampling uses uniform spanning column subsets and a uniform v, with rank-rejection success P_A(1)/2^D.
claims.caveat: No cheap matrix acquisition, recognition, or expanded-input validation claimed; no arbitrary-sampler hardness.
